question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the parabola parametrized by $r(t)=2t\,i+(2-{t}^{2})\,j$ for $t\in [0,1].$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2t,\,y(t)=2-{t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-{t}^{2})\,j \\  & =2\,i-2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}]dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t+2-{t}^{2})\cdot 2+2t\cdot (-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-6{t}^{2}+4t+4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-2{t}^{3}+2{t}^{2}+4t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-2+2+4)-0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
